title: The Core Facilitator holds broad discretion to resolve Atlas ambiguities and contradictions by interpretation
content:
A.1.1.2.1 authorizes the Core Facilitator "to conduct Atlas Interpretations to address and resolve ambiguities or contradictions within Atlas Documents," including "providing expanded definitions for problematic terms, clarifying the practical application of specific rules or logic, and similar actions." It grounds this in the Core Council's Broad Discretionary Capacity (A.0.1.2.1).

The supporting annotations sharpen the two triggers into distinct failure modes: **ambiguity** (A.1.1.2.1.0.3.1) is where one document's language admits multiple readings, while **contradiction** (A.1.1.2.1.0.3.2) is where *different* Atlas documents conflict with each other. The first is an internal defect of text; the second is an emergent defect of a large document tree that no single author controls.

The architectural choice is to route both to an operational role rather than to a vote. Governance cycles are slow and adversarial; ambiguity and contradiction are discovered continuously and often mid-execution. Vesting repair in the Core Facilitator keeps the Atlas usable in real time.

The cost is obvious and is why the guardrails are stacked around it: an actor empowered to supply "expanded definitions" for problematic terms can, in principle, redefine its way to a preferred outcome. Mandatory documentation, precedent congruence, and codification into the Element Annotation and Facilitator Action Precedent types are what keeps that power narrow in practice rather than in theory.
description: A.1.1.2.1 authorizes expanded definitions, clarified application of rules, and similar measures — placing textual repair inside a facilitator role rather than requiring a governance vote.
